hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis, surgery, or treatment goes wrong at a clinic or hospital serving Dorris, the aftermath can leave you and your family scrambling for answers. We can help you understand California's medical malpractice rules and explore your options at no cost.

about.title: Dorris Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Dorris sits in a rural stretch of Siskiyou County, and residents here often travel outside the immediate area for specialized medical care, which can add layers of complexity when something goes wrong. Whether the issue involved a missed diagnosis at a local clinic, a medication error, or a surgical complication at a regional hospital, sorting out what happened requires medical records, timelines, and often a qualified expert to review the care you received. California law puts real deadlines and procedural steps in front of anyone pursuing this kind of claim, and a bad medical outcome by itself doesn't automatically mean malpractice occurred. We listen to what happened and evaluate your situation under California's specific rules for medical injury claims. There's no charge for an initial consultation.

items.title: Strict Filing Windows Apply
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a malpractice claim. We can help you understand where you stand on that timeline before options close.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Is Required First
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires sending the healthcare provider a 90-day notice of intent. Missing or mishandling this step can delay or derail a valid claim.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, these cases typically require a qualified medical expert to establish that the care fell below an accepted standard. We can help arrange that kind of review.

items.question: I live in Dorris — do I need to find a local attorney?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because Dorris is a small community in Siskiyou County, the attorney best suited to your case may practice elsewhere in the region or even further away, especially if your care happened at a larger hospital outside town. We can help you find an attorney experienced in California malpractice claims regardless of where their office sits.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened, whichever comes first. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth having someone review your specific timeline soon rather than waiting.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover?
items.answer: California law caps non-economic damages (things like pain and suffering) in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, like medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves risk, and an unfavorable result doesn't by itself prove negligence occurred. A qualified medical expert typically needs to review the case and confirm that the care fell below an accepted standard before a claim can move forward.
